draft.title: Co-interior angles
card: A transversal is a line that crosses other lines. Co-interior angles are on the same side of the transversal and between the two lines. They make a C shape.
When the two lines are parallel, co-interior angles add to 180°. So one angle = 180° − the other.
Example: one co-interior angle is 115°. The other is 180° − 115° = 65°.
This also works as a test. If a pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°, the lines are parallel. If it does not, they are not parallel.
draft.remember: Co-interior angles in a C shape add to 180° when the lines are parallel.

a.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 78°. What is the other co-interior angle?
a.why: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to 180°, so 180° − 78° = 102°. 78° is wrong because that would be the rule for equal angles, not co-interior ones.
a.clue: The two angles in a C shape add to a straight angle.

b.q: A transversal crosses two lines. A pair of co-interior angles measures 112° and 70°. What does this show?
opts: The lines are parallel, as 112° is obtuse
b.why: 112° + 70° = 182°, not 180°. Co-interior angles add to 180° only when the lines are parallel, so these lines are not parallel.
b.clue: Add the two angles and compare the total with 180°.
